verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati isigilismiṁ pabbate.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Isigili Mountain.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

verses.pali: “Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ vebhāraṁ pabbatan”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, do you see that Mount Vebhāra?”

verses.pali: “Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, vebhārassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti.
verses.english: “It used to have a different label and description.

verses.pali: Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ paṇḍavaṁ pabbatan”ti?
verses.english: Do you see that Mount Paṇḍava?”

verses.pali: “Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, paṇḍavassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti.
verses.english: “It too used to have a different label and description.

verses.pali: Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ vepullaṁ pabbatan”ti?
verses.english: Do you see that Mount Vepulla?”

verses.pali: “Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, vepullassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti.
verses.english: “It too used to have a different label and description.

verses.pali: Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ gijjhakūṭaṁ pabbatan”ti?
verses.english: Do you see that Mount Vulture’s Peak?”

verses.pali: “Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, gijjhakūṭassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti.
verses.english: “It too used to have a different label and description.

verses.pali: Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, imaṁ isigiliṁ pabbatan”ti?
verses.english: Do you see that Mount Isigili?”

verses.pali: “Imassa kho pana, bhikkhave, isigilissa pabbatassa esāva samaññā ahosi esā paññatti.
verses.english: “It used to have exactly the same label and description.

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, pañca paccekabuddhasatāni imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsino ahesuṁ.
verses.english: Once upon a time, five hundred Independent Buddhas dwelt for a long time on this Isigili.

verses.pali: Te imaṁ pabbataṁ pavisantā dissanti, paviṭṭhā na dissanti.
verses.english: They were seen entering the mountain, but after entering were seen no more.
When people noticed this they said:
That’s how it came to be known as Isigili, the “seer-swallower”.
I shall declare the names of the Independent Buddhas;
I shall extol the names of the Independent Buddhas;
I shall teach the names of the Independent Buddhas.

verses.pali: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
“Ariṭṭho nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
verses.english: “The independent Buddhas who dwelt for a long time on this Isigili were named Ariṭṭha,

verses.pali: upariṭṭho nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
tagarasikhī nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
yasassī nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
sudassano nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
piyadassī nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
gandhāro nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
piṇḍolo nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
upāsabho nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
nīto nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
tatho nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi,
sutavā nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi;
bhāvitatto nāma, bhikkhave, paccekasambuddho imasmiṁ isigilismiṁ pabbate ciranivāsī ahosi.

verses.english: Those saintly beings, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope,
the supreme men, free of thorns.
Independent Buddhas, enders of the leash to existence;
and Hiṅgū and Hiṅga the mighty.
Two sages named Jāli, and Aṭṭhaka;
then the awakened one Kosala, then Subāhu;
right and true, stainless and astute.
Kāḷa and Upakāḷa, Vijita and Jita,

verses.pali: Aṅgo ca paṅgo ca guttijito ca;
verses.english: Aṅga and Paṅga, and Guttijita too;
Passin gave up attachment, suffering’s root,
Manomaya, and Bandhumā the cutter of conceit,
then Adhimutta, and Ketumā the immaculate.
another sage, Sayha of peerless effort.
There are twelve Ānandas, Nandas, and Upanandas,
and Bhāradvāja, bearing his final body.
Tissa and Upatissa, <j>who’ve both cut the bonds to rebirth,
Upasīdarī and Sīdarī, who’ve both cut off craving.
Maṅgala was awakened, free of greed,
Usabha cut the net, the root of suffering,
Upanīta who attained the state of peace,
Mānatthaddha, beautiful and free of greed,
and the Buddha Kaṇha, his mind well freed.
These and other mighty ones <j>awakened independently,
enders of the leash to existence—
honor these great seers <j>who have slipped all chains,
